answer.rationale: Constraints prune the field before memory does. rollback_release is closed by compliance regardless of how well memory_b1 worked on day 18. regional_failover (memory_b2) succeeded during a latency degradation, but that episode is not this one: we are at settlement peak with heavy writes, and shifting regions mid-peak puts in-flight writes at risk, which directly violates the 'without losing customer writes' half of the objective. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) contained a failing external dependency; here the write path itself is degrading, so failing fast would shed exactly the customer writes we are told to preserve. add_capacity (memory_b3) is attractive but the archived success was provisioning headroom BEFORE the peak; provisioning during a 90-minute-old climb likely lands after the window closes. That leaves route_read_replicas: memory_b5 is the only inherited record where the observed outcome was specifically write-path latency recovery caused by taking read load off the primary, which matches the current symptom. I want the two source records that carry the most weight: memory_b5 because my whole choice rests on it (I need to know whether the write-latency recovery was actually attributed to the replica routing or merely coincided with it, and whether the load profile resembled a settlement peak), and memory_b3 because if provisioning was in fact fast rather than pre-staged, add_capacity becomes the stronger play and I should switch. Scale is a small guarded test, not a broad rollout: I am mid-incident at peak with one intervention available, so I route a bounded slice of report/dashboard reads first with a fast revert path, and widen only on a confirmed primary-load drop. Downstream value risk: read replicas serve stale data, so any settlement, reconciliation, balance, or limit check that silently lands on a replica could make correct-looking but wrong money decisions, and that error would propagate into ledgers rather than showing up as latency. Routing must be restricted to reporting/dashboard queries with financial-truth reads pinned to the primary. Residual uncertainty is real: these memories are consolidated summaries whose successes were each recorded under conditions that differ from three-way concurrent pressure, none of them was logged at settlement peak, and if the climb is driven by lock contention or write amplification from the new build rather than read contention, read offload will not touch the cause and I will have spent the window. I hold that possibility open rather than treating memory_b5 as settled.
